title: Scalar Gaussian threshold disagreement
statement: Let $t,\theta\in\mathbb R$ with $\cos\theta>0$, and let $X,Y$ be independent standard Gaussian variables. The probability that exactly one of $X\le t$ and $\cos\theta\,X+\sin\theta\,Y\le t$ holds is $\displaystyle\int_{\mathbb R}\left|\Phi\!\left(\frac{t-\sin\theta\,y}{\cos\theta}\right)-\Phi(t)\right|\,d\gamma(y)$, where $\gamma$ and $\Phi$ are the standard Gaussian measure and distribution function.
replaced: Let $\Phi,\varphi$ denote the standard Gaussian distribution function and density. For $t,y\in\mathbb R$, define $q_{t,y}(\theta)=\Phi((t-\sin\theta\,y)/\cos\theta)-\Phi(t)$. If $\cos\theta>0$ and $X,Y$ are independent standard Gaussian variables, then $\Pr(1_{(-\infty,t]}(X)\ne1_{(-\infty,t]}(\cos\theta\,X+\sin\theta\,Y))=\mathbb E_Y|q_{t,Y}(\theta)|$.
